svg.title: Where memory can be kept
svg.desc: Three places a memory can be kept, side by side. Text outside the model: notes, facts or a profile, pasted into the prompt; a person can read it, one fact can be corrected or deleted, and it works with any model, including a hosted one; reading it costs prompt tokens on every request. Internal state of the model: cached keys and values or memory vectors that the model attends to; nobody can read it, a single fact can rarely be deleted, and it needs access to the model's internals; reading it costs a pass over the cache. Weights: knowledge written into the parameters by editing or training; nobody can read it, a single fact cannot be deleted, and it needs the weights; reading it costs nothing extra, writing it costs training or an edit. Under the three, a note: a vector store is text memory, because its embeddings are only an index, and the model reads the text that the search finds.
svg.text: The same fact can be kept as text, as internal state of the model, or in its weights. The form decides who can read it and
